PullRequest.Title: Fix backslash escaping in MarkdownString.appendLink
PullRequest.Body:
`MarkdownString.appendLink` considered a `)`, `]` or `"` delimiter escaped whenever it directly followed a backslash. With an even run of backslashes (e.g. `\\)`), Markdown pairs the backslashes and the delimiter stays active, so the link target could end the generated link early.

Changes:
- `MarkdownString._escape` treats a delimiter as escaped only after an odd number of backslashes, and completes a trailing odd backslash run so it cannot escape the closing delimiter that `appendLink` adds.
- The editor link hover no longer marks the whole hover as trusted. A `command:` link only enables the command it targets (`enabledCommands`); other links render untrusted.

## How to test
- Unit tests: `scripts/test --run src/vs/base/test/common/markdownString.test.ts --run src/vs/base/test/browser/markdownRenderer.test.ts` → 196 passing, 2 pending. The two new tests fail without the `_escape` change.
- Manually in Code OSS: an HTML `href` containing `\\)` followed by more Markdown link syntax now shows a single "Follow link" whose target is the whole URL.
- An extension-provided `command:` document link still runs from the hover and on Ctrl+click.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` and ESLint on the changed files pass.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The regex backtracking behavior and synchronous call path are explicit. The built-in link computer accepts backslashes in detected URLs, decoration creation eagerly calls appendLink for every returned link, and models up to 50 MB are eligible. Only the prevalence and exact stall duration of very long runs are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: regular-expression matching and backtracking CPU work on the renderer/UI thread
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For maximum consecutive backslash-run length k not immediately followed by the escaped delimiter, matching grows as O(k^2); total refresh cost sums this work across all detected links.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: quadratic CPU growth and blocked UI-thread latency during link-decoration refresh
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous `new RegExp(delimiter, 'g')` scanned each target linearly and invoked the replacement only for actual delimiters, so non-delimiter backslash runs did not trigger repeated suffix scans.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Escaping now searches for every possible start of a backslash run and greedily consumes the remaining run before testing for a delimiter or end-of-string.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 109 replaces the prior delimiter-only global regex with `(\\*)(delimiter|$)`, introducing a greedy backslash quantifier before an alternative that commonly fails.
Findings.Title: Avoid quadratic backtracking in link escaping
Findings.Impact: Opening or editing a generated or crafted document containing an auto-detected URL with a long backslash run can block the editor UI while link decorations are installed; a single sufficiently long run can cause seconds of CPU work rather than scaling with document length.
Findings.Evidence: For a URL segment containing k consecutive backslashes followed by an ordinary character, `\\*` first consumes all k characters, `(delimiter|$)` fails, and the engine backtracks across the run. The unanchored global search then retries at the next backslash, doing k+(k-1)+... work. `LinkDetector.updateDecorations` synchronously calls `LinkOccurrence.decoration` -> `getHoverMessage` -> `MarkdownString.appendLink` for every detected link after providers return; the default link computer treats backslash as a valid in-link character.
Findings.Recommendation: Implement the parity handling as a single forward scan, or match non-overlapping backslash runs and delimiters without retrying every suffix, preserving odd/even and trailing-run semantics in O(value.length).

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening or editing a document with detected links, then installing link decorations and hover text.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On model open or a debounced content change, all link providers must complete before updateDecorations synchronously constructs hover markdown for every effective link on the UI thread. The new regex is therefore on the critical path from provider completion to usable updated link decorations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize/inspect the model in the editor worker and return all auto-detected links.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One web-worker request per eligible model refresh for the built-in provider; other registered providers are also invoked once each and merged before decoration work. The escaping regression then runs once per effective merged link, not once per provider result duplicate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider and worker request occurred before the diff; after it returned, appendLink escaped each target with a delimiter-only linear scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider requests must finish before decorations are updated, but the reported quadratic CPU work occurs synchronously after the boundary returns and directly delays UI progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective link count after provider union, each target length, and especially the maximum consecutive backslash-run length k; the introduced work is O(k^2) for a run followed by a non-delimiter.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Language link providers run concurrently through Promise.all; the built-in provider makes one worker request for the whole model. Once results are merged, hover construction and decoration installation are serialized on the UI thread with no yield or limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Link hovers are rebuilt whenever all link decorations are refreshed; there is no cold/warm cache for escaped hover strings. Provider debounce coalesces edits, but it does not cache or coalesce the synchronous per-link escaping after results arrive.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the greedy quantifier retries every suffix of a failed backslash run, and the full synchronous call path from returned links to appendLink is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long consecutive backslash runs are uncommon in normal hand-written URLs, and exact stall duration depends on V8 and run length. Generated or crafted files are accepted up to the 50 MB model-sync limit, so the trigger is concrete even though prevalence is uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity CPU regression: the diff changes linear escaping into quadratic regex backtracking on a valid link-target character sequence on the UI-thread refresh path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Constructing markdown links for chat, terminal, remote-session, notification, and tool UI surfaces.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: String escaping must finish before the caller can return or render its markdown. There are no filesystem, subprocess, database, IPC, or network calls inside appendLink; it is synchronous CPU and allocation work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Target, label, and optional title lengths, number of appendLink calls, and longest consecutive backslash run before an ordinary character.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each call is synchronous and serialized in its caller. Collection callers may invoke it repeatedly, so costs add across displayed messages, links, or tool entries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: MarkdownString.appendLink performs escaping eagerly for every call and has no result cache. Cold and warm behavior are identical; callers own any higher-level reuse.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the shared helper's quadratic mechanism; medium for frequency of pathological inputs outside the editor-link path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most application-generated URIs contain no long backslash runs, so ordinary calls remain near-linear. Extension-, tool-, or content-derived labels and targets can be large, but their typical maximum sizes vary by caller.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same shared regression is covered by the reported finding; no separate finding is needed because it has the identical changed line and mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Creating trusted options for editor command-link hovers.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After providers complete, getHoverMessage parses each string command URL while building decorations. This is synchronous but remains a linear parse alongside existing toString, regex, replace, and appendLink scans.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Obtain document links from built-in and contributed providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The pre-existing provider calls are once per registered provider per model refresh and merged before each effective command link is processed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same providers and merge behavior ran before the diff; only local trust metadata construction changed afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider completion gates hover creation; the diff does not add or multiply any boundary call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective command-link count after provider union and command URL length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider collection remains concurrent; command URL parsing and hover creation are serialized per effective link on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Command-link hover options are regenerated with decoration options; no parsed-URI cache is used. The new parse occurs only for string command URLs, while URI instances reuse their path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the parse is new and linear; high that it does not create boundary fan-out or superlinear scaling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Command links in editor documents are provider-dependent, but even large counts only add one linear local URI parse per string command link.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance finding: the added URI.parse is bounded linear local work and does not materially amplify the existing per-link hover construction or provider boundaries.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files. Submitted one high-confidence UI-thread CPU finding for quadratic regex backtracking; rejected the local command URI parse and test-only changes as non-reportable.
